rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. This tests a simple RNA-only model with PCA encoding and single-profile setting, isolating the effect of RNA data alone. It provides foundational performance metrics to compare against more complex multimodal configurations later.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with PCA achieves 0.48 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (same RNA encoder, no image data), clarifying whether multiprofile settings improve performance. It isolates the effect of profile aggregation while keeping RNA encoder consistent, addressing key uncertainty about profile settings' impact.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001) for RNA-only models. This experiment tests transformer aggregation (vs. avgpool in config_002) to isolate the effect of aggregation method on multiprofile RNA-only models. It balances exploitation of the multiprofile advantage with exploration of aggregation techniques, which are critical for model performance.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002: 0.590664) outperforms singleprofile and transformer aggregation. This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 with scvi_n200 RNA encoder in the high-performing multiprofile/avgpool setup, isolating the effect of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the multiprofile/avgpool direction with exploration of encoder variations, which could reveal if scvi_n200 improves accuracy further.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and multiprofile setting (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.650124). This experiment tests whether combining this RNA encoder with image data (resnet50) using avgpool aggregation (same as config_005) can further improve performance. It isolates the effect of adding image modality while keeping RNA and aggregation settings consistent, balancing exploitation of current strengths and exploration of multimodal potential.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and resnet50 achieve 0.6315 accuracy (config_030), but fusion method (concat vs weighted) remains untested. This experiment tests whether weighted fusion improves performance compared to concat, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It balances exploitation of the scvi_n200 + resnet50 combination (already showing strong performance) with exploration of critical design choices.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with the more advanced imagenet_vit_l image encoder while keeping other parameters the same would further improve accuracy. It isolates the effect of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision, and builds on the promising direction of weighted fusion and scvi_n200 RNA encoder.

The existing evidence shows that config_037 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.706). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other components the same, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It is the best use of the remaining budget to either confirm or improve upon the current top performer.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt (a more advanced model) while keeping the effective multimodal setup could further improve performance. It clarifies if the RNA encoder choice is a critical factor, leveraging the remaining budget to explore a promising direction with minimal design changes.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, ViT-L image encoder, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with ViT-L image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_049), which isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice while maintaining the high-performing image encoder and fusion strategy. It directly compares scgpt (lower-performing in config_051) against scvi_n200, addressing uncertainty about RNA encoder impact on multimodal performance.
